sections.note: Oz had no SLA policies and White Rabbit had no mappings. QA created non-default 'CM-REVIEW-20261026-08 final-b MSP policy' (24/7 fallback schedule; P1 30m/60m, P2 4m/240m; default 50/75/90/100% thresholds) assigned only to the White Rabbit client. Alice created two Medium tickets.
White Rabbit 'Medium' → Oz 'P1 - Critical'. Manage SLA policies link opened SLA settings.

sections.section: 2. Start a new MSP obligation on escalation
sections.note: Customer and MSP views show 'White Rabbit IT SLA: No SLA configured' separately from 'Oz SLA' with due times.
Mapping changed to P2; ticket 1 kept 30/60 and identical dueAt timestamps; ticket 2 captured 4/240.

sections.section: 4. Pause MSP responsibility without erasing history
sections.note: Handback → pauseReasons [customer_responsible], both views 'Paused'; customer re-escalation resumed the same obligation (generation 1, targets unchanged, elapsed time preserved).

Kansas Farms (terminated) ticket had no MSP obligation, so a read-only supplement used guide 10's terminated Accept-7 relationship whose ticket had one: customer keeps its ticket without an Oz SLA panel; QA cannot open it. Ticket 2 (QA assigned) produced 50/75/90/100% events; recipients only QA; SMTP sink: 'SLA Warning: … at 90%' and 'SLA BREACH: … Response SLA Exceeded' to qa@emeraldcity.oz only; Alice received only her ticket-created mail.

Mapping restored to Not mapped and policy unassigned from White Rabbit through the UI (before: no mappings, no client policy; after: same). Disposable non-default policies remain (referenced by obligations).

actors.name: departed-customer-admin
actors.organization: CM-REVIEW-20261026-01 Accept-7 (customer, terminated by guide 10; supplement only, read-only)

steps: QA opens Co-managed SLA priorities, then Manage SLA policies; creates disposable policy assigned to White Rabbit
QA maps Medium → P1, saves, reloads
Alice escalates ticket 1; both views show Oz SLA; handoff history
QA maps Medium → P2; ticket 1 targets unchanged; Alice escalates ticket 2 (4-minute response)
QA assigns ticket 2's MSP assignment to QA
QA returns ticket 1 to customer; both views paused; Alice re-escalates
Kansas Farms admin and QA departed-relationship read checks
Wait for ticket 2 response breach; inspect notifications, QA bell and SMTP sink
outcomes: Mapping change did not rewrite ticket 1 dueAt
Handback paused with history; re-escalation resumed same obligation
Breach notices delivered to the MSP assignee only (in-app + email)
Mapping and client policy back to original
limitations: Departure-with-live-clock evidence is the read-only supplement on another agent's terminated relationship (Kansas Farms ticket had no prior MSP obligation).
Business-hours (non-24/7) arithmetic not exercised: policy used the 24/7 fallback schedule.
Escalated disposable attempt/final tickets remain open with obligations; their breach notices also reached QA.
notes: Published recording recording-combined is a lossless concat of recording (sections prep-5b) and supplement-departed-clock-readonly (section 5a departed clock), composed by the lead so every claimed flow is in the published WebM.
